messages.subject: Bitmaps as layers
parts:
I am rather new to ggplot2 but the elegance of the graphics is
compelling. I am currently plotting where different groups of patients
live in my local area using RgoogleMaps but the ability to do much
more than crude placement of points or lines on the map is very
frustrating after having used ggplot2.

Unfortunately my corner of the world is not well represented in an R
dataset so the standard way of displaying the territory with coord_map
is not much help. What would be great would be to put a map tile
bitmap as a layer in a ggplot2 graphic - is there a way or am I going
to have to hack it in SVG??

This is not just a cartographic issue for example if I wanted to plot
the frequency of fractures as circles of varying size on a bitmap of
the skeleton I would be in the same situation.

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: Bitmaps as layers
parts:
Hi,

You could use the pixmap or EBImage package to import the bitmap into
R. This data can then be plotted with ggplot2 using geom_tile(). The
only problem with this approach is that it's rather slow for high
resolution images. A quick and dirty workaround I suggested here a few
months ago was to plot the image as a background using Grid, then
adding your layers on top (a dummy example follows). The inconvenient
here is that you need to be very careful about the scaling of your map
with respect to the axes.

require(RGraphics)
require(EBImage)

ebimageGrob <-
function (pic, x=0.5, y=0.5, ...)
{
dims <- dim(pic)
colours = t(channel(pic, "x11"))
colours <- colours[ rev(seq_len(nrow(colours))), ]
width = unit(dims[1], "points")
height = unit(dims[2], "points")
vp <-
viewport(x=x, y=y)
child <-
imageGrob(dims[2], dims[1], col=colours, gp=gpar(col=colours),
by=FALSE, vp=vp, ...)

gTree(width= convertUnit(width, "in", val=TRUE),
height=convertUnit(height, "in", val=TRUE),
children=gList(child), cl="ebimage")

}

pic <- readImage("http://blog.meebo.com/imgs/map.png")
#g1 <- ebimageGrob(pic)
#dev.new(width=g1$width, height=g1$height)
#grid.draw(g1)

background = function(){
ebimageGrob(pic)

}

dsmall <- diamonds[sample(nrow(diamonds), 100), ]
str(dsmall)
d <- ggplot(dsmall, aes(carat, price)) +
geom_point()+
opts(panel.background = background)

Note that this second approach can be further improved using the
grid.raster() function of R-devel.

HTH,

baptiste
